moments.title: x + 5 = 15
moments.summary: Early in the school year, the student works through a timed set of 15 multiplication, division and algebra problems, finishing on time and asking for help on one algebra item (the tutor reminds them that the opposite of subtraction is addition). The tutor then opens an algebra review: a variable is just a placeholder, and to solve for it you do the opposite operation. Asked how to find x in x + 5 = 15, the student pauses for 20 seconds and says "I don't know."
moments.hint: This is an appropriate place for rigor because the student has shown mastery of a skill so if the tutor pushes for rigor here the student could deepen their understanding so they are able to apply this skill to other problems.

moments.title: Missing vertices of a rectangle
moments.summary: A lesson on finding the missing coordinates of rectangles and squares. The student starts out unsure ("like two maybe?" for an x-coordinate), and the tutor has been walking through each problem with small questions (which point lines up, which number comes first), plotting points together when needed. On a new rectangle with two missing vertices, the student has just found an x-coordinate, −3, by looking at the point on the left.
moments.hint: This is an appropriate time for scaffolding as the tutor is still working with the student to understand how to use what they know to find the missing coordinates.
